data.bug_class: heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read of DCT coefficient blocks)
data.rationale: In decompress_smooth_data (jdcoefct.c), the block column loop runs from master->first_MCU_col[ci] to master->last_MCU_col[ci]. These limits are computed in jdapistd.c:237-241 from the (possibly scaled) output width and can exceed the component's allocated width_in_blocks - 1. last_block_column is set to width_in_blocks - 1 (line 578), but the accesses at lines 586-597 read prev_prev_block_row[1]/[2], prev_block_row[1]/[2], buffer_ptr[1]/[2], next_block_row[1]/[2] and next_next_block_row[1]/[2] guarded only by 'block_num < last_block_column' / 'block_num + 1 < last_block_column' while block_num itself can be >= width_in_blocks, so buffer_ptr points past the last allocated block in the virtual-array row and [1]/[2] read beyond the allocation. Reachability: the fuzz target (fuzz/decompress.cc, LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput) calls tjDecompress2 with TJFLAG_LIMITSCANS on attacker data; for a progressive JPEG, when no AC data is present for a scan, jdcoefct.c:65 selects decompress_smooth_data (block smoothing is on by default). Narrow images (component plane width <= 8 blocks) combined with IDCT scaling (harness iteration pfi==1 uses half width/height) make last_MCU_col exceed width_in_blocks, triggering the out-of-bounds read. This matches the known libjpeg-turbo progressive/block-smoothing buffer overrun in 2.1 beta.
